title.zh: 卷九 列傳第三: 侯瑱 歐陽頠 吳明徹 裴子烈
title.en: Volume 9: Hou Tian; Ouyang Wei; Wu Mingche; Pei Zilie
title.raw: 卷九 列傳第三: 侯瑱 歐陽頠 吳明徹 裴子烈 Volume 9: Hou Tian; Ouyang Wei; Wu Mingche; Pei Zilie

sentences.zh: 陳書卷九

translations.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 9
translations.idiomatic: Book of Chen, Volume 9

sentences.zh: 列傳第三

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Three
translations.idiomatic: Biographies, Part Three

sentences.zh: 侯瑱 歐陽頠子紇 吳明徹裴子烈

translations.literal: Hou Tian; Ouyang Wei, son He; Wu Mingche; Pei Zilie
translations.idiomatic: Hou Tian; Ouyang Wei, son He; Wu Mingche; Pei Zilie

sentences.zh: 侯瑱字伯玉，巴西充國人也。

translations.literal: Hou Tian, styled Boyu, was a native of Chongguo in Baxi.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Tian, styled Boyu, came from Chongguo in Baxi.

sentences.zh: 父弘遠，世為西蜀酋豪。

translations.literal: His father Hongyuan for generations had been a chieftain of western Shu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hongyuan's house had been chieftains in western Shu for generations.

sentences.zh: 蜀賊張文萼據白崖山，有红萬人，梁益州刺史鄱陽王蕭範命弘遠討之。

translations.literal: The Shu bandit Zhang Wene held White Cliff Mountain with troops numbering ten thousand; Liang Inspector of Yizhou the Prince of Poyang Xiao Fan ordered Hongyuan to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu rebel Zhang Wene held White Cliff Mountain with ten thousand troops. Xiao Fan, Prince of Poyang and inspector of Yizhou, sent Hongyuan against him.

sentences.zh: 弘遠戰死，瑱固請復讎，每戰必先鋒陷陣，遂斬文萼，由是知名。

translations.literal: Hongyuan died in battle; Tian firmly asked to take revenge, in every fight charging first into the breach, and at last beheaded Wene—by this he became known.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyuan fell in battle. Tian begged to avenge him, led every charge himself, and at last struck off Wene's head—after that his name was known.

sentences.zh: 因事範，範委以將帥之任，山谷夷獠不賓附者，嵭遣瑱征之。

translations.literal: Through serving Fan, Fan entrusted him with commanders' duties; whenever valley Yi and Liao in the mountains would not submit, he always sent Tian to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Fan won his trust as a field commander; whenever mountain Yi and Liao would not submit, Fan sent Tian to bring them in.

sentences.zh: 累功授輕車府中兵參軍、晉康太守。

translations.literal: By accumulated merit he was made Central Army Major in the Light Chariots Office and Administrator of Jinkang.
translations.idiomatic: Merit piled up until he was made central-army major in the Light Chariots Office and administrator of Jinkang.

sentences.zh: 範為雍州刺史，瑱除超武將軍、馮翊太守。

translations.literal: When Fan became Inspector of Yongzhou, Tian was made Supernal Martial General and Administrator of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan became inspector of Yongzhou, Tian was made supernal-martial general and administrator of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 範遷鎮合肥，瑱又隨之。

translations.literal: When Fan moved his garrison to Hefei, Tian again followed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan shifted his garrison to Hefei, Tian went with him.

sentences.zh: 侯景圍臺城，範乃遣瑱輔其世子嗣，入援京邑。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing besieged the Terrace City, Fan then sent Tian to assist his heir Sih in relieving the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing besieged the Terrace City, Fan sent Tian to help his heir Sih relieve the capital.

sentences.zh: 京城陷，瑱與嗣退還合肥，仍隨範徙鎮湓城。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, Tian and Sih withdrew to Hefei and still followed Fan in moving the garrison to Pencheng.
translations.idiomatic: The capital fell. Tian and Sih fell back to Hefei and followed Fan when he moved the garrison to Pencheng.

sentences.zh: 俄而範及嗣皆卒，瑱領其红，依于豫章太守莊鐵。

translations.literal: Before long both Fan and Sih died; Tian took over their troops and attached himself to Zhuang Tie, Administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Fan and Sih both died. Tian took their troops and threw in with Zhuang Tie, administrator of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 鐵疑之，瑱懼不自安，詐引鐵謀事，因而刃之，據有豫章之地。

translations.literal: Tie suspected him; Tian feared and could not rest easy, pretended to summon Tie to discuss affairs, and thus killed him with a blade, seizing the territory of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Tie mistrusted him. Tian, uneasy, lured Tie under pretense of counsel and killed him, seizing Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 侯景將于慶南略地至豫章，城邑皆下，瑱窮蹙，乃降於慶。

translations.literal: Hou Jing's general Yu Qing when campaigning south reached Yuzhang; the cities all fell; Tian was hard pressed and then surrendered to Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing's general Yu Qing marched south to Yuzhang and took every town. Hard pressed, Tian surrendered to Qing.

sentences.zh: 慶送瑱於景，景以瑱與己同姓，託為宗族，待之甚厚，留其妻子及弟為質。

translations.literal: Qing sent Tian to Jing; Jing, because Tian bore the same surname, treated him as a clansman, received him very generously, and kept his wife, children, and younger brother as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Qing sent Tian to Jing. Jing claimed kinship by surname, treated him lavishly, and kept his wife, children, and younger brother as hostages.

sentences.zh: 遣瑱隨慶平定蠡南諸郡。

translations.literal: He sent Tian to follow Qing in pacifying the Li-man south of Lihu.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Tian with Qing to pacify the Li country south of Lihu.

sentences.zh: 及景敗於巴陵，景將宋子仙、任約等嵭為西軍所獲，瑱乃誅景黨與，以應

translations.literal: When Jing was defeated at Baling, Jing's generals Song Zixian and Ren Yue were all captured by the Western armies; Tian then executed Jing's partisans to answer
translations.idiomatic: When Jing was broken at Baling, his generals Song Zixian and Ren Yue were all taken by the loyal western armies. Tian executed Jing's partisans to join

translations.literal: (Our)
translations.idiomatic: (our)

sentences.zh: [義]軍，[1]景亦盡誅其弟及妻子。

translations.literal: the Loyalist armies. Editorial footnote marker 1. Jing also executed Tian's younger brother and wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: the loyalist armies. [1] Jing in turn put Tian's brother, wife, and children to death.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝授瑱武臣將軍、南论州刺史，郫縣侯，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang appointed Tian Martial Retainer General, Inspector of South Yu, Marquis of Pixian, fief one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang made him martial-retainer general and inspector of South Yu, Marquis of Pixian, fief one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 仍隨都督王僧辯討景，恆為前鋒，每戰劔敵。

translations.literal: He still followed the commander-in-chief Wang Sengbian in campaigning against Jing, always as vanguard, in every battle gaining the advantage.
translations.idiomatic: He still followed Wang Sengbian against Jing as vanguard and carried every fight.

sentences.zh: 既復臺城，景奔吳郡，僧辯使瑱率兵追之，與景戰於吳松江，大敗景，盡獲其軍實。

translations.literal: After the Terrace City was recovered, Jing fled to Wu commandery; Sengbian sent Tian to lead troops in pursuit; he fought Jing on the Wu Song River, utterly defeated Jing, and took all his military stores.
translations.idiomatic: When the Terrace City was retaken Jing fled to Wu. Sengbian sent Tian in pursuit; on the Wu Song River he shattered Jing and seized all his stores.

sentences.zh: 進兵錢塘，景將謝答仁、呂子榮等皆降。

translations.literal: Advancing to Qiantang, Jing's generals Xie Daren, Lü Zirong, and others all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to Qiantang. Jing's generals Xie Daren, Lü Zirong, and the rest surrendered.

sentences.zh: 以功除南豫州刺史，鎮于姑熟。

translations.literal: For merit he was made Inspector of South Yu and garrisoned at Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was made inspector of South Yu and garrisoned Gushu.

sentences.zh: 承聖二年，齊遣郭元建出自濡須，僧辯遣瑱領甲士三千，築壘於東關以扞之，大敗元建。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chengsheng, Qi sent Guo Yuanjian out from Ruxu; Sengbian sent Tian to lead three thousand armored men, build a fort at Dong Pass to resist him, and utterly defeated Yuanjian.
translations.idiomatic: In Chengsheng year 2 Qi sent Guo Yuanjian from Ruxu. Sengbian sent Tian with three thousand armored men to fortify Dong Pass; he broke Yuanjian completely.

sentences.zh: 除使持節、鎮北將軍，[2]給鼓吹一部，增邑二千戶。

translations.literal: He was made Bearer of the Staff, Pacifier of the North General, Editorial footnote marker 2. given one set of martial music, fief increased by two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He received the staff as pacifier-of-the-north general [2], one suite of martial music, and two thousand more households in his fief.

sentences.zh: 西魏來寇荊州，王僧辯以瑱為前軍，赴援，未至而荊州陷。

translations.literal: When Western Wei came to raid Jingzhou, Wang Sengbian made Tian vanguard to go to the rescue; he had not arrived when Jingzhou fell.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei raided Jingzhou. Sengbian made Tian vanguard of the relief force, but Jingzhou fell before he arrived.

sentences.zh: 瑱之九江，因纫晉安王還都。

translations.literal: Tian went to Jiujiang and because of it escorted the Prince of Jin'an back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Tian went to Jiujiang and escorted the Prince of Jin'an back to court.

sentences.zh: 承制以瑱為侍中、使持節、都督江晉吳齊四州諸軍事、江州刺史，改封康樂縣公，邑五千戶，進號車騎將軍。

translations.literal: By imperial commission he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary, Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Jiang, Jin, Wu, and Qi, Inspector of Jiangzhou, enfeoffed Duke of Kangle county, fief five thousand households, advanced to Chariots-and-Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: By regency commission he was attendant-in-ordinary, bearer of the staff, commander of Jiang, Jin, Wu, and Qi, inspector of Jiangzhou, Duke of Kangle, fief five thousand households, promoted to chariots-and-cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 司徒陸法和據郢州，引齊兵來寇，乃使瑱都督红軍西討，未至，法和率其部北度入齊。

translations.literal: Minister of State Lu Fahe held Yingzhou and drew Qi troops to raid; Tian was then made commander of the army westward; before he arrived Fahe led his command north across the river into Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Fahe, minister of state, held Yingzhou and called in Qi. Tian was ordered west against him, but Fahe crossed north into Qi before he came up.

sentences.zh: 齊遣慕容恃德鎮于夏首，瑱控引西還，水陸攻之，恃德食盡，請和，瑱還鎮豫章。

translations.literal: Qi sent Murong Shide to garrison at Xiashou; Tian drew the western lines back and attacked by land and water; Shide's food ran out and he asked for peace; Tian returned to garrison Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Qi sent Murong Shide to Xiashou. Tian pulled the western front back and attacked by land and water until Shide's stores were gone and he sued for peace. Tian returned to Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 僧辯使其弟僧愔率兵與瑱共討蕭勃，及高祖誅僧辯，僧愔陰欲圖瑱而奪其軍，瑱知之，盡收僧愔徒黨，僧愔奔齊。

translations.literal: Sengbian sent his younger brother Sengyin with troops to join Tian in campaigning against Xiao Bo; when the Founder executed Sengbian, Sengyin secretly wished to plot against Tian and seize his army; Tian knew it, seized all Sengyin's partisans, and Sengyin fled to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian sent his brother Sengyin with troops to join Tian against Xiao Bo. When the Founder killed Sengbian, Sengyin meant to take Tian's army. Tian knew it, rounded up Sengyin's men, and Sengyin fled to Qi.

sentences.zh: 紹泰二年，以本號加開府儀同三司，餘並如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaotai, with his former title he was given the Grand Precedence of the Palace, all else as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaotai year 2 he kept his rank and was given grand precedence of the palace; the rest unchanged.

sentences.zh: 是時，瑱據中流，兵甚彊盛，又以本事王僧辯，雖外示臣節，未有入朝意。

translations.literal: At that time Tian held the middle Yangzi and his troops were very strong; moreover he had long served Wang Sengbian; though outwardly he showed the forms of a subject, he had no mind to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: Tian then held the middle river, his troops very strong, and he had served Sengbian long. He bowed in form but would not come to court.

sentences.zh: 初，余孝頃為豫章太守，及瑱鎮豫章，乃於新吳縣別立城柵，與瑱相拒。

translations.literal: Earlier Yu Xiaoding had been Administrator of Yuzhang; when Tian garrisoned Yuzhang he then at Xinwu county separately built a walled stockade to resist Tian.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xiaoding had been administrator of Yuzhang. When Tian garrisoned there, Xiaoding built a separate walled camp at Xinwu to hold him off.

sentences.zh: 瑱留軍人妻子於豫章，令從弟奫知後事，悉红以攻孝頃。

translations.literal: Tian left the troops' wives and children at Yuzhang, ordered his cousin Shen to manage rear affairs, and sent all his troops to attack Xiaoding.
translations.idiomatic: Tian left the troops' families at Yuzhang, put his cousin Shen in charge of the rear, and sent every soldier against Xiaoding.

sentences.zh: 自夏及冬，弗能克，乃長圍守之，盡收其禾稼。

translations.literal: From summer to winter he could not take it; he then made a long siege and gathered in all the grain.
translations.idiomatic: From summer through winter he could not break it. He settled into a long siege and stripped the fields bare.

sentences.zh: 奫與其部下俟方兒不協，[3]方兒怒，率所部攻奫，虜掠瑱軍府妓妾金玉，歸于高祖。

translations.literal: Shen was at odds with his subordinate Hou Fang'er; Editorial footnote marker 3. Fang'er in anger led his command to attack Shen, plundered the women, jewels, and gold of Tian's headquarters, and went over to the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: Shen fell out with his man Hou Fang'er. [3] Fang'er in rage attacked Shen, looted Tian's headquarters of women, jewels, and gold, and went to the Founder.

sentences.zh: 瑱既失根本，兵红皆潰，輕歸豫章，豫章人拒之，乃趨湓城，投其將焦僧度。

translations.literal: Tian having lost his base, the troops all scattered; he lightly returned to Yuzhang; the people of Yuzhang refused him; he then hurried to Pencheng and threw himself on his general Jiao Songdu.
translations.idiomatic: Baseless, his troops broke. He slipped back to Yuzhang; the town shut him out. He ran to Pencheng and sought Jiao Songdu.

sentences.zh: 僧度勸瑱投齊，瑱以高祖有大量，必能容己，乃詣闕請罪，高祖復其爵位。

translations.literal: Songdu urged Tian to go over to Qi; Tian thought the Founder was magnanimous and would surely spare him; he then came to the palace to beg pardon, and the Founder restored his rank and fief.
translations.idiomatic: Songdu urged him toward Qi. Tian judged the Founder magnanimous and went to court to beg pardon. The Founder restored rank and fief.

sentences.zh: 永定元年，授侍中、車騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongding he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Chariots-and-Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongding year 1 he was made attendant-in-ordinary and chariots-and-cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 二年，進位司空。

translations.literal: In the second year he was advanced to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he rose to minister of works.

sentences.zh: 王琳至於沌口，周文育、侯安都嵭沒，乃以瑱為都督西討諸軍事。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin reached Dundu, Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu were both drowned; Tian was then made Commander-in-Chief of the Western Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lin reached Dundu, Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu were both lost in the river. Tian was made commander of the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 瑱至于梁山。

translations.literal: Tian reached Liangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Tian reached Liangshan.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，進授太尉，增邑千戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne he was further made Grand Commandant, fief increased by one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne Tian was made grand commandant with one thousand more households.

sentences.zh: 王琳至于柵口，又以瑱為都督，侯安都等嵭隸焉。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin reached Zhakou, Tian was again made commander; Hou Andu and the others were all under his command.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin reached Zhakou Tian was again commander; Hou Andu and the rest served under him.

sentences.zh: 瑱與琳相持百餘日，未決。

translations.literal: Tian and Lin faced each other for more than a hundred days without decision.
translations.idiomatic: Tian and Lin locked for more than a hundred days without a decision.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年二月，東關春水稍長，舟艦得通，琳引合肥漅湖之红，舳艫相次而下，其勢甚盛。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Tiancheng, the spring waters at Dong Pass rose a little; ships could pass; Lin drew the troops of Chaohu at Hefei; war vessels followed one after another downriver; the momentum was very strong.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancheng year 1, second month, spring flood at Dong Pass let ships through. Lin brought Chaohu troops from Hefei downstream in a long line of war craft—the weight of it was immense.

sentences.zh: 瑱率軍進獸檻洲，[4]琳亦出船列于江西，隔洲而泊。

translations.literal: Tian led the army to advance to Beast-Barrier Isle; Editorial footnote marker 4. Lin also brought out ships and arrayed them on the west of the river, moored across the isle from them.
translations.idiomatic: Tian advanced to Beast-Barrier Isle. [4] Lin ranged his fleet on the west bank across the isle.

sentences.zh: 明日合戰，琳軍少劔，退保西岸。

translations.literal: The next day they joined battle; Lin's army had little advantage and withdrew to hold the west bank.
translations.idiomatic: They fought the next day. Lin gained little and pulled back to the west bank.

sentences.zh: 及夕，東北風大起，吹其舟艦，舟艦嵭壞，沒于沙中，溺死者數十百人。

translations.literal: By evening a northeast wind rose greatly and blew his ships; the ships were all wrecked, sunk in the sand; those drowned numbered in the tens and hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk a northeast gale wrecked his fleet in the shallows. Tens and hundreds drowned.

sentences.zh: 浪大不得還浦，夜中又有流星墜于賊營。

translations.literal: The waves were too great to return to the harbor; in the night a falling star also dropped into the rebel camp.
translations.idiomatic: Waves blocked the harbor. That night a meteor fell in the rebel camp.

sentences.zh: 及旦風靜，琳入浦治船，以荻船塞於浦口，又以鹿角繞岸，不敢復出。

translations.literal: When dawn came the wind was calm; Lin entered the harbor to repair ships, blocked the mouth with reed boats, and also ringed the shore with antlers; he did not dare come out again.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the wind fell. Lin crept into harbor, choked the mouth with reed boats, ringed the shore with antlers, and would not come out.

sentences.zh: 是時，西魏遣大將軍史寧躡其上流，瑱聞之，知琳不能持久，收軍劔據湖浦，以待其敝。

translations.literal: At that time Western Wei sent the great general Shi Ning to press upriver; Tian heard it and knew Lin could not last, gathered the army and firmly held Lake Pu to wait for his exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei sent Shi Ning upriver. Tian knew Lin could not hold, drew off, and camped on Lake Pu to wait him out.

sentences.zh: 及史寧至，圍郢州，琳恐红潰，乃率船艦來下，去蕪湖十里而泊，擊柝聞於軍中。

translations.literal: When Shi Ning arrived and besieged Yingzhou, Lin feared his troops would scatter; he then led the fleet downriver, moored ten li from Wuhu, and the night-watch sounded through the camp.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ning besieged Yingzhou. Lin, fearing collapse, came downstream and moored ten li from Wuhu; watches sounded all night.

sentences.zh: 明日，齊人遣兵數萬助琳，琳引红向梁山，欲越官軍以屯險要。

translations.literal: The next day Qi sent tens of thousands of troops to aid Lin; Lin led the troops toward Liangshan, wishing to pass the government army and hold a strategic point.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Qi sent tens of thousands to help. Lin marched toward Liangshan to slip past the loyal army and seize a strong point.

sentences.zh: 齊儀同劉伯球率兵萬餘人助琳水戰，行臺慕容恃德子子會領鐵騎二千，在蕪湖西岸博望山南，為其聲勢。

translations.literal: Qi's Yitong Liu Boqiu led more than ten thousand men to aid Lin in river fighting; Xingtai Murong Shide's son Zihui led two thousand iron cavalry on the south of Bowang Mountain on the west bank of Wuhu to lend him force.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's Yitong Liu Boqiu brought ten thousand for the river fight. Murong Shide's son Zihui held two thousand horse on Bowang Mountain west of Wuhu as a screen.

sentences.zh: 瑱令軍中晨炊蓐食，分搥盪頓蕪湖洲尾以待之。

translations.literal: Tian ordered the army to cook at dawn and take bed-meals, divide mallets and sweep to halt at the tail of Wuhu Isle and wait for them.
translations.idiomatic: Tian had the men cook at dawn, eat from their mats, and mass at the tail of Wuhu Isle.

sentences.zh: [5]將戰，有微風至自東南，红軍施拍縱火。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 5. About to fight, a light breeze came from the southeast; the loyal army set rams and loosed fire.
translations.idiomatic: [5] As battle neared, a light wind rose from the southeast. The loyal fleet set rams and fire.

sentences.zh: 定州刺史章昭達乘平虜大艦，中江而進，發拍中于賊艦，其餘冒突、青龍，各相當值。

translations.literal: Dingzhou Inspector Zhang Zhaoda rode the Level-Barbarians great ship straight up the mid-river, launched rams and struck the rebel ships; the rest—assault craft and Green Dragons—each took their match.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhaoda of Dingzhou drove the Level-Barbarians in midstream, smashed rebel hulls with rams; assault craft and Green Dragons paired off ship for ship.

sentences.zh: 又以牛皮冒蒙衝小船，以觸賊艦，並鎔鐵灑之。

translations.literal: They also covered rush boats in oxhide, used them to strike rebel ships, and also poured molten iron.
translations.idiomatic: Oxhide-sheathed rush boats rammed the rebels; molten iron rained down.

sentences.zh: 琳軍大敗。

translations.literal: Lin's army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's army was shattered.

sentences.zh: 其步兵在西岸者，自相蹂踐，馬騎嵭淖于蘆荻中，笃馬脫走以免者十二三。

translations.literal: His infantry on the west bank trampled one another; horsemen were all mired in the reeds; only one or two in ten of tethered horses broke loose and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Infantry on the west bank trampled each other. Horse sank in the reeds; only one or two in ten broke their tethers and fled.

sentences.zh: 盡獲其舟艦器械，赠禽齊將劉伯球、慕容子會，自餘俘馘以萬計。

translations.literal: They took all his ships and gear, captured alive the Qi generals Liu Boqiu and Murong Zihui; the rest of prisoners and heads numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: They seized every ship and weapon, took Liu Boqiu and Murong Zihui alive, and counted prisoners and heads by the ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 琳與其黨潘純鲶等乘單舴艋冒陣走至湓城，猶欲收合離散，红無附者，乃與妻妾左右十餘人入齊。

translations.literal: Lin with his partisans Pan Chunnian and others took a single skiff and burst through the line to flee to Pencheng; he still wished to gather the scattered; no troops would follow; he then with wife, concubines, and a dozen attendants entered Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Lin, Pan Chunnian, and a few others broke out in one skiff to Pencheng, tried to rally the broken, found no troops would follow, and crossed to Qi with wife, concubines, and a dozen attendants.

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 6.
translations.idiomatic: See editorial note 6.

sentences.zh: 其年，詔以瑱為都督湘、巴、郢、江、吳等五州諸軍事，鎮湓城。

translations.literal: That year an edict made Tian Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Xiang, Ba, Ying, Jiang, Wu, and the other five provinces, garrisoning Pencheng.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was ordered commander of Xiang, Ba, Ying, Jiang, Wu, and four other provinces, garrisoning Pencheng.

sentences.zh: 周將賀若敦、獨孤盛等寇巴、湘，又以瑱為西討都督，與盛戰於西江口，大敗盛軍，虜其人馬器械，不可勝數。

translations.literal: When Zhou generals He Ruo Dun and Dugu Sheng raided Ba and Xiang, Tian was again made commander of the western campaign; he fought Sheng at West River Mouth, utterly defeated Sheng's army, and captured men, horses, and gear beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's He Ruo Dun and Dugu Sheng raided Ba and Xiang. Tian was western commander again, broke Sheng at West River Mouth, and took men, horses, and gear past counting.

sentences.zh: 以功授使持節、都督湘桂郢巴武沅六州諸軍事、湘州刺史，改封零陵郡公，邑七千戶，餘如故。

translations.literal: For merit he was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of Xiang, Gui, Ying, Ba, Wu, and Yuan, Inspector of Xiangzhou, enfeoffed Duke of Lingling commandery, fief seven thousand households, the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he received the staff, command of six provinces, inspectorship of Xiangzhou, dukedom of Lingling, fief seven thousand households; the rest unchanged.

sentences.zh: 二年，以疾表求還朝。

translations.literal: In the second year, because of illness he memorialized asking to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 illness drove him to ask leave for the capital.

sentences.zh: 三月，於道薨，時年五十二。

translations.literal: In the third month he died on the road, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the road in the third month, aged fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、驃騎大將軍、大司馬，加羽葆、鼓吹、班闰二十人，給東園祕器，諡曰壯肅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Attendant-in-Ordinary, Rapid Cavalry General, Grand Marshal, with feather canopy, martial music, twenty sword-guards in the procession, Eastern Garden secret rites, posthumous title Zhuangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was attendant-in-ordinary, rapid-cavalry general, grand marshal, with feather canopy, martial music, twenty sword-guards, Eastern Garden rites, posthumous name Zhuangsu.

sentences.zh: 其年九月，配享高祖廟庭。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year he was given place in the Founder's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: That ninth month he entered the Founder's temple.

sentences.zh: 子淨藏嗣。

translations.literal: His son Jingzang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingzang succeeded.

sentences.zh: 淨藏尚世祖第二女富陽公主，以公主除員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Jingzang married Emperor Wen's second daughter the Princess of Fuyang; because of the princess he was made Extraordinary Cadet of the Dispersed Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzang married Emperor Wen's second daughter, the Princess of Fuyang, and by that match was made extraordinary cadet of the dispersed cavalry.

sentences.zh: 太建三年卒，贈司徒主簿。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taijian he died; posthumously made Registrar of the Minister of State.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Taijian year 3 and was posthumously registrar to the minister of state.

sentences.zh: 淨藏無子，弟就襲封。

translations.literal: Jingzang had no son; his younger brother Jiu inherited the fief.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzang had no son; his brother Jiu inherited the fief.

sentences.zh: 歐陽頠字靖世，長沙臨湘人也。

translations.literal: Ouyang Wei, styled Jingshi, was a native of Linxiang in Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Wei, styled Jingshi, came from Linxiang in Changsha.

sentences.zh: 為郡豪族。

translations.literal: He was a great clan of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His house was a great clan of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖景達，梁代為本州治中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jingda in the Liang generation was Administrator of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jingda had been the commandery administrator under Liang.

sentences.zh: 父僧寶，屯騎校尉。

translations.literal: His father Sengbao was Commandant of Escort Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sengbao was commandant of escort cavalry.

sentences.zh: 頠少質直有思理，以言行篤信著聞於嶺表。

translations.literal: Wei in youth was plain and upright and had powers of thought; by conduct and speech of deep trust he was known beyond the mountain passes.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was plain, upright, and thoughtful; south of the passes he was known for trustworthy conduct.

sentences.zh: 父喪毀瘠甚至。

translations.literal: At his father's death he was wasted by grief to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: His father's death wasted him with grief.

sentences.zh: 家產累積，悉讓諸兄。

translations.literal: The family's accumulated wealth he entirely yielded to his elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He gave the family's accumulated wealth entirely to his elder brothers.

sentences.zh: 州郡頻辟不應，乃廬於麓山寺傍，專精習業，博通經史。

translations.literal: The province and commandery repeatedly summoned him but he would not respond; he then built a hut beside Lushan Temple, devoted himself to study, and broadly mastered the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Province and commandery summoned him in vain. He built a hut by Lushan Temple, studied hard, and mastered classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 年三十，其兄逼令從宦，起家信武府中兵參軍，遷平西邵陵王中兵參軍事。

translations.literal: At thirty his elder brother forced him to enter office; he began as Central Army Major in the Trustworthy Martial Office and was transferred to Central Army Major on the staff of the Prince of Shaoling, General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: At thirty his brother forced him into service: central-army major in the Trustworthy Martial Office, then on the staff of the Prince of Shaoling, general who pacifies the west.

sentences.zh: 梁左纫將軍蘭欽之少也，與頠相善，故頠常隨欽征討。

translations.literal: Liang's Left Rapid General Lan Qin in his youth was friendly with Wei; therefore Wei often followed Qin on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was close to Liang's left-rapid general Lan Qin and often campaigned with him.

sentences.zh: 欽為衡州，仍除清遠太守。

translations.literal: When Qin was made Inspector of Hengzhou, Wei was still made Administrator of Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin became inspector of Hengzhou, Wei was made administrator of Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 欽南征夷獠，擒陳文徹，所獲不可勝計，獻大銅鼓，累代所無，頠預其功。

translations.literal: Qin campaigned south against the Yi and Liao, captured Chen Wenche; the booty could not be counted; he presented a great bronze drum such as no generation had had; Wei shared in the merit.
translations.idiomatic: Qin marched south against Yi and Liao, took Chen Wenche, and seized booty past counting, including a great bronze drum none had seen. Wei shared the credit.

sentences.zh: 還為直閤將軍，仍除天門太守，伐蠻左有功。

translations.literal: Returning he was made Direct Attendant General and still made Administrator of Tianmen; campaigning against the southern Man he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he was direct-attendant general and administrator of Tianmen; against the southern Man he won merit.

sentences.zh: 刺史廬陵王蕭續深嘉之，引為賓客。

translations.literal: Inspector the Prince of Luling Xiao Xu deeply praised him and took him as a client.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Luling, inspector Xiao Xu, prized him and took him as client.

sentences.zh: 欽征交州，復啟頠同行。

translations.literal: When Qin campaigned against Jiaozhou he again asked Wei to go with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin marched on Jiaozhi he asked Wei along again.

sentences.zh: 欽度嶺以疾終，頠除臨賀內史，啟乞送欽喪還都，然後之任。

translations.literal: Qin crossed the mountains and died of illness; Wei was made Interior Minister of Linhe; he memorialized asking to send Qin's coffin back to the capital and only then take up his post.
translations.idiomatic: Qin died crossing the ridge. Wei was made interior minister of Linhe, begged to send the coffin home first, then take office.

sentences.zh: 時湘衡之界五十餘洞不賓，队令衡州刺史韋粲討之，粲委頠為都督，悉皆平殄。

translations.literal: At that time more than fifty caves on the border of Xiang and Heng would not submit; the order still went to Inspector of Hengzhou Wei Can to campaign against them; Can entrusted Wei as commander and all were pacified and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: More than fifty caves between Xiang and Heng would not submit. Wei Can, inspector of Hengzhou, put Wei in command and wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 粲啟梁武，稱頠誠幹，降詔讣賞，仍加超武將軍，征討廣、衡二州山賊。

translations.literal: Can memorialized to Liang Wu, praising Wei's sincerity and ability; an edict came down with rewards; he was still made Supernal Martial General to campaign against the mountain bandits of Guang and Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Can praised his loyalty and skill to Emperor Wu of Liang. Rewards came down; he was made supernal-martial general against the mountain bandits of Guang and Heng.

sentences.zh: 侯景構逆，粲自解還都征景，以頠監衡州。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing hatched rebellion, Can removed himself and returned to the capital to campaign against Jing; he left Wei to oversee Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, Can went back to fight him and left Wei to oversee Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 京城陷後，嶺南互相吞併，蘭欽弟前高州刺史裕攻始興內史蕭紹基，[7]奪其郡。

translations.literal: After the capital fell, south of the mountains they devoured one another; Lan Qin's younger brother the former Inspector of Gaozhou Yu attacked the Interior Minister of Shixing Xiao Shaoji; Editorial footnote marker 7. and seized his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital fell the south tore itself apart. Qin's brother Yu, former inspector of Gaozhou, attacked Shixing interior minister Xiao Shaoji [7] and seized his commandery.

sentences.zh: 裕以兄欽與頠有舊，遣招之，頠不從。

translations.literal: Yu, because his elder brother Qin and Wei were old friends, sent to recruit him; Wei would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, remembering Qin's friendship with Wei, sent to recruit him. Wei refused.

sentences.zh: 乃謂使云：「高州昆季隆顯，莫非國恩，今應赴難援都，豈可自為跋扈。

translations.literal: He then told the envoy: "The brothers of Gaozhou have risen high—all is the state's grace; now one should hurry to aid the capital in its peril—how can one play the bully on one's own?"
translations.idiomatic: He told the envoy: "Gaozhou's brothers owe their rank to the throne. They should march to save the capital—not play petty kings."

sentences.zh: 」及高祖入援京邑，將至始興，頠乃深自結託。

translations.literal: When the Founder came to relieve the capital and was about to reach Shixing, Wei then bound himself to him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder marched to relieve the capital and neared Shixing, Wei threw in with him wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 裕遣兵攻頠，高祖援之，裕敗，高祖以王懷明為衡州刺史，遷頠為始興內史。

translations.literal: Yu sent troops to attack Wei; the Founder aided him; Yu was defeated; the Founder made Wang Huaiming Inspector of Hengzhou and moved Wei to Interior Minister of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Yu attacked; the Founder helped Wei and broke Yu. Wang Huaiming took Hengzhou; Wei was moved to interior minister of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 高祖之討蔡路養、李遷仕也，頠率兵度嶺，以助高祖。

translations.literal: When the Founder campaigned against Cai Luyang and Li Qianshi, Wei led troops across the mountains to aid the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: On the Founder's campaigns against Cai Luyang and Li Qianshi, Wei crossed the ridge with troops to help.

sentences.zh: 及路養等平，頠有功，梁元帝承制以始興郡為東衡州，以頠為持節、通直散騎常侍、都督東衡州諸軍事、雲麾將軍、東衡州刺史，新豐縣伯，邑四百戶。

translations.literal: When Luyang and the others were pacified, Wei had merit; Emperor Yuan of Liang by regency commission made Shixing commandery into East Hengzhou and made Wei Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant for Direct Communication, Commander-in-Chief of East Hengzhou, Cloud-Banner General, Inspector of East Hengzhou, Baron of Xinfeng county, fief four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When they were pacified he won merit. Emperor Yuan made Shixing into East Hengzhou and gave Wei the staff, direct-communication attendant, command of East Hengzhou, cloud-banner general, inspectorship, barony of Xinfeng, fief four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 侯景平，元帝遍問朝宰：「今天下始定，極須良才，卿各舉所知。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified, Emperor Yuan asked all the court ministers everywhere: "Now the realm is newly settled; we urgently need good men—each of you recommend whom you know."
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing fell, Emperor Yuan asked the court: "The realm is new-settled. Name the men you trust."

sentences.zh: 」戝臣未有對者。

translations.literal: The ministers had none who answered.
translations.idiomatic: No one spoke.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「吾已得一人。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have already got one man."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I already have one man."

sentences.zh: 」侍中王讣進曰：「未審為誰？

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Chan advanced and said: "I do not yet know who it is?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chan stepped forward: "Who is it?"

sentences.zh: 」帝云：「歐陽頠公正有匡濟之才，恐蕭廣州不肯致之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Ouyang Wei is upright and has talent to steady the age; I fear the Inspector of Guangzhou Xiao will not be willing to send him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Ouyang Wei is upright and can steady the age—but Guangzhou's Xiao may not let him go."

sentences.zh: 」[8]乃授武州刺史，尋授郢州刺史，欲令出嶺，蕭勃留之，不獲拜命。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 8. He then appointed Inspector of Wuzhou; soon he appointed Inspector of Yingzhou, wishing to have him leave the mountains; Xiao Bo detained him and he could not take up the commission.
translations.idiomatic: [8] He was made inspector of Wuzhou, then of Yingzhou, to draw him out of the hills. Xiao Bo held him and he never took up the seal.

sentences.zh: 尋授使持節、散騎常侍、都督衡州諸軍事、忠武將軍、衡州刺史，進封始興縣侯。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Bearer of the Staff, Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of Hengzhou, Loyal Martial General, Inspector of Hengzhou, advanced to Marquis of Shixing county.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he had the staff, scattered-cavalry attendant, command of Hengzhou, loyal-martial general, inspectorship, and was advanced to Marquis of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 時蕭勃在廣州，兵彊位重，元帝深患之，遣王琳代為刺史。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Bo was at Guangzhou, troops strong and position weighty; Emperor Yuan deeply feared him and sent Wang Lin to replace him as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Bo at Guangzhou was strong and heavy. Emperor Yuan feared him and sent Wang Lin to replace him.

sentences.zh: 琳已至小桂嶺，勃遣其將孫瑒監州，盡率部下至始興，避琳兵鋒。

translations.literal: Lin had already reached Little Gui Ridge; Bo sent his general Sun Yang to oversee the province, led all his subordinates to Shixing, and avoided Lin's edge.
translations.idiomatic: Lin reached Little Gui Ridge. Bo sent Sun Yang to hold the province, drew all his men to Shixing, and shied from Lin's edge.

sentences.zh: 頠別據一城，不往謁勃，閉門高壘，亦不拒戰。

translations.literal: Wei separately held one city, did not go to call on Bo, shut the gates and built high ramparts, and also did not resist fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Wei held a separate city, would not call on Bo, shut the gates, piled the ramparts, and would not fight.

sentences.zh: 勃怒，遣兵襲頠，盡收其貲財馬仗。

translations.literal: Bo was angry and sent troops to strike Wei, seizing all his wealth, horses, and arms.
translations.idiomatic: Bo in rage sent troops, seized all his wealth, horses, and arms.

sentences.zh: 尋赦之，還復其所，復與結盟。

translations.literal: Soon he pardoned him, restored what was his, and again made alliance with him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he pardoned him, restored his goods, and swore alliance again.

sentences.zh: 荊州陷，頠委質於勃。

translations.literal: When Jingzhou fell, Wei pledged himself to Bo.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzhou fell, Wei pledged to Bo.

sentences.zh: 及勃度嶺出南康，以頠為前軍都督，頓豫章之苦竹灘，周文育擊破之，擒送于高祖，高祖釋之，深加接待。

translations.literal: When Bo crossed the mountains and came out to Nankang, he made Wei commander of the vanguard army, stationed at Bitter Bamboo Ford in Yuzhang; Zhou Wenyü broke him, captured him, and sent him to the Founder; the Founder released him and received him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Bo crossed to Nankang and made Wei vanguard at Bitter Bamboo Ford in Yuzhang. Zhou Wenyü broke him, sent him to the Founder, who freed him and treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 蕭勃死後，嶺南擾亂，頠有聲南土，且與高祖有舊，乃授頠使持節、通直散騎常侍、都督衡州諸軍事、安南將軍、衡州刺史，始興縣侯。

translations.literal: After Xiao Bo died, south of the mountains was disturbed; Wei had a name in the southern lands and moreover was old friends with the Founder; he was then made Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant for Direct Communication, Commander-in-Chief of Hengzhou, Pacifier of the South General, Inspector of Hengzhou, Marquis of Shixing county.
translations.idiomatic: After Bo died the south was in turmoil. Wei was known there and was the Founder's old friend—so he received the staff, direct-communication attendant, command of Hengzhou, pacifier-of-the-south general, inspectorship, and marquisate of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 未至嶺南，頠子紇已克定始興。

translations.literal: Before he reached south of the mountains, Wei's son He had already pacified Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Before he crossed the ridge, his son He had already taken Shixing.

sentences.zh: 及頠至嶺南，皆懾伏，仍進廣州，盡有越地。

translations.literal: When Wei reached south of the mountains, all were awed and submitted; he still advanced to Guangzhou and wholly possessed the Yue lands.
translations.idiomatic: South of the ridge all submitted in awe. He pressed on to Guangzhou and held all Yue.

sentences.zh: 改授都督廣交越成定明新高合羅愛建德宜黃利安石雙十九州諸軍事、鎮南將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史，持節、常侍、侯並如故。

translations.literal: He was changed to Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Guang, Jiao, Yue, Cheng, Ding, Ming, Xin, Gao, He, Luo, Ai, Jiande, Yihuang, Li'an, Shishuang, and the other nineteen provinces, General Who Pacifies the South, General of the Center Who Pacifies Yue, Inspector of Guangzhou; Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant, and Marquis all as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commander of nineteen southern provinces, general who pacifies the south, center-general who pacifies Yue, inspector of Guangzhou; staff, attendant, and marquisate unchanged.

sentences.zh: 王琳據有中流，頠自海道及東嶺奉使不絕。

translations.literal: Wang Lin held the middle Yangzi; Wei by sea route and the eastern ridge sent envoys without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin held the middle river. Wei kept envoys moving by sea and the eastern passes.

sentences.zh: 永定三年，進授散騎常侍，增都督衡州諸軍事，即本號開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongding he was advanced to Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, increased command of Hengzhou military affairs, and with his former title given Grand Precedence of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongding year 3 he was advanced to scattered-cavalry attendant, given more command over Hengzhou, and grand precedence with his old title.

sentences.zh: 世祖嗣位，進號征南將軍，改封陽山郡公，邑一千五百戶，又給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne he was advanced to General Who Campaigns South, changed to Duke of Yangshan commandery, fief one thousand five hundred households, and again given one set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded he was made general who campaigns south, Duke of Yangshan, fief fifteen hundred households, with martial music again.

sentences.zh: 初，交州刺史袁曇緩密以金五百兩寄頠，令以百兩還合浦太守龔蒍，[9]四百兩付兒智矩，餘人弗之知也。

translations.literal: Earlier Inspector of Jiaozhou Yuan Tanhuan had secretly sent Wei five hundred taels of gold, ordering one hundred taels returned to Administrator of Hepu Gong Ai; Editorial footnote marker 9. four hundred taels given to his son Zhiju—others did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yuan Tanhuan of Jiaozhi had secretly left Wei five hundred taels of gold—one hundred for Hepu administrator Gong Ai [9], four hundred for his son Zhiju—unknown to anyone else.

sentences.zh: 頠尋為蕭勃所破，貲財嵭盡，唯所寄金獨在。

translations.literal: Wei was soon broken by Xiao Bo; his wealth was all gone; only the deposited gold remained.
translations.idiomatic: Bo soon broke him and stripped him bare—only the entrusted gold remained.

sentences.zh: 曇緩亦尋卒，至是頠嵭依信還之，時人莫不嘆伏。

translations.literal: Tanhuan also soon died; at this Wei was able faithfully to return it; men of the time all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Tanhuan died too. Wei returned every ounce faithfully, and men marveled.

sentences.zh: 其重然諾如此。

translations.literal: Such was his weight on promises.
translations.idiomatic: That was how he kept his word.

sentences.zh: 時頠弟盛為交州刺史，次弟邃為衡州刺史，合門顯貴，名振南土。

translations.literal: At that time Wei's younger brother Sheng was Inspector of Jiaozhou, his next younger brother Sui Inspector of Hengzhou; the whole house was illustrious, their name shaking the southern lands.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Sheng held Jiaozhi, Sui held Hengzhou—the whole clan shone, their fame ringing through the south.

sentences.zh: 又多致銅鼓、生口，獻奉珍異，前後委積，頗有助於軍國焉。

translations.literal: They also repeatedly sent bronze drums and captives, presented rare tribute; before and after it piled up and greatly aided the army and state.
translations.idiomatic: They sent bronze drums, captives, and rare tribute in heaps that greatly fed army and state.

sentences.zh: 頠以天嘉四年薨，時年六十六。

translations.literal: Wei in the fourth year of Tiancheng died, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Wei died in Tiancheng year 4, aged sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、車騎大將軍、司空、廣州刺史，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary, Chariots-and-Cavalry General, Minister of State, Inspector of Guangzhou, posthumous title Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously: attendant-in-ordinary, chariots-and-cavalry general, minister of state, inspector of Guangzhou, posthumous name Mu.

sentences.zh: 子紇嗣。

translations.literal: His son He succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son He succeeded.

sentences.zh: 紇字奉聖，頗有幹略。

translations.literal: He, styled Fengsheng, had considerable ability and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He, styled Fengsheng, had talent and nerve.

sentences.zh: 天嘉中，除黃門侍郎、員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the Tiancheng era he was made Yellow Gate Gentleman and Extraordinary Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiancheng era he was yellow-gate gentleman and extraordinary scattered-cavalry attendant.

sentences.zh: 累遷安遠將軍、衡州刺史。

translations.literal: By repeated promotion he was made Pacifier of the Distance General and Inspector of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to pacifier-of-the-distance general and inspector of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 襲封陽山郡公，都督交廣等十九州諸軍事、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: He inherited the dukedom of Yangshan commandery, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Jiao, Guang, and the other nineteen provinces, Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited Yangshan, commanded nineteen provinces including Jiao and Guang, and inspected Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 在州十餘年，威惠著於百越，進號輕車將軍。

translations.literal: More than ten years in the province; his might and kindness were known among the Hundred Yue; he was advanced to Light Chariots General.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years in the province his power and kindness were known among the Hundred Yue; he was advanced to light-chariots general.

sentences.zh: 光大中，上流蕃鎮嵭多懷貳，高宗以紇久在南服，頗疑之。

translations.literal: In the Guangda era, garrisons of the upper Yangzi mostly harbored second thoughts; Emperor Xuan, because He had long served in the south, quite suspected him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangda era upper-Yangzi garrisons wavered. Emperor Xuan, knowing He had ruled the south long, mistrusted him.

sentences.zh: 太建元年，下詔徵紇為左纫將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taijian an edict summoned He to be Left Rapid General.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 1 an edict recalled him as left-rapid general.

sentences.zh: 紇懼，未欲就徵，其部下多勸之反，遂舉兵攻衡州刺史錢道戢。

translations.literal: He was afraid and did not wish to obey the summons; many of his subordinates urged him to rebel; he then raised troops and attacked Inspector of Hengzhou Qian Daoji.
translations.idiomatic: He feared the summons. His men urged revolt. He attacked Qian Daoji, inspector of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 道戢告變，乃遣儀同章昭達討紇，屢戰兵敗，執送京師，伏誅，時年三十三。

translations.literal: Daoji reported the emergency; they then sent Yitong Zhang Zhaoda to campaign against He; after repeated battles the troops were defeated; he was seized and sent to the capital, executed by beheading, aged thirty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji raised the alarm. Zhang Zhaoda was sent against him. After repeated defeats He was taken to the capital and beheaded at thirty-three.

sentences.zh: 家口籍沒。

translations.literal: His household was registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: His household was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 子詢以年幼免。

translations.literal: His son Xun because of young age was spared.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun was spared for youth.

sentences.zh: 吳明徹字通昭，[10]秦郡人也。

translations.literal: Wu Mingche, styled Tongzhao; Editorial footnote marker 10. was a native of Qin commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mingche, styled Tongzhao [10], came from Qin commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖景安，齊南譙太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jing'an was Administrator of Nanqiao in Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jing'an had been administrator of Nanqiao under Qi.

sentences.zh: 父樹，梁右軍將軍。

translations.literal: His father Shu was Liang Right Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shu was Liang's right-guard general.

sentences.zh: 明徹幼孤，性至孝，年十四，感墳塋未備，家貧無以取給，乃勤力耕種。

translations.literal: Mingche was orphaned young, nature utmost filial; at fourteen, moved that the tombs were not yet prepared and the family was poor without means to supply it, he then labored hard at planting.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was filial beyond measure. At fourteen, seeing the graves unprepared and the house too poor to furnish them, he farmed with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 時天下亢旱，苗稼燋枯，明徹哀憤，每之田中，號泣，仰天自訴。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was in great drought; the seedlings were scorched dry; Mingche grieved and was angry; every time he went to the fields he wept and cried out to heaven in appeal.
translations.idiomatic: Drought scorched the fields. He wept in the furrows and cried to heaven.

sentences.zh: 居數日，有自田還者，云苗已更生，明徹疑之，謂為紿己，及往田所，竟如其言。

translations.literal: After several days someone returning from the fields said the seedlings had sprouted anew; Mingche doubted it, thinking himself deceived; when he went to the field place, it was exactly as the man had said.
translations.idiomatic: After days a neighbor said the grain had greened again. Mingche did not believe it—until he walked the field and found it true.

sentences.zh: 秋而大穫，足充葬用。

translations.literal: In autumn the harvest was great, enough to complete the burial.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the harvest filled the burial need.

sentences.zh: 時有伊氏者，善占墓，謂其兄曰：「君葬之日，必有乘白馬逐鹿者來經墳所，此是最小孝子大貴之徵。

translations.literal: At that time a certain Master Yi was skilled at reading tombs; he told Mingche's elder brother: "On the day you bury, there will surely come one riding a white horse chasing a deer to pass the grave site—this is the omen of the youngest filial son attaining great honor."
translations.idiomatic: A diviner named Yi told his brother: "On burial day a man on a white horse chasing a deer will pass the mound—that is the sign of the youngest son's greatness."

sentences.zh: 」至時果有此應，明徹即樹之最小子也。

translations.literal: When the time came there was indeed this response; Mingche was Shu's youngest son.
translations.idiomatic: It happened as foretold. Mingche was Shu's youngest son.

sentences.zh: 起家梁東宮直後。

translations.literal: He began office as Eastern Palace Direct Attendant of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He began as direct attendant in Liang's eastern palace.

sentences.zh: 及侯景寇京師，天下大亂，明徹有粟麥三千餘斛，而讫里饑餧，乃白諸兄曰：「當今草竊，人不圖久，柰何有此而不與鄉家共之？

translations.literal: When Hou Jing raided the capital the realm was in great disorder; Mingche had more than three thousand bushels of grain and millet while the whole village was starving; he then told his elder brothers: "In this age of grass-bandits men do not plan far—how can we keep this and not share with our neighbors?"
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing struck the capital the land was chaos. Mingche had three thousand bushels while the village starved. He told his brothers: "Bandits roam; men live day to day—how can we hoard and not share with the lane?"

sentences.zh: 」於是計口平分，同其豐儉，戝盜聞而避焉，賴以存者甚红。

translations.literal: He then divided by mouths, sharing alike in plenty or want; grass-bandits heard and avoided them; those who lived by it were very many.
translations.idiomatic: He divided by mouths, rich and poor alike. Bandits heard and passed them by; many lived because of it.

sentences.zh: 及高祖鎮京口，深相要結，明徹乃詣高祖，高祖為之降階，執手即席，與論當世之務。

translations.literal: When the Founder garrisoned Jingkou he bound himself deeply with Mingche; Mingche then came to the Founder; the Founder for him descended a step, took his hand and sat at once, and discussed affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder held Jingkou they bound themselves close. Mingche came to him; the Founder stepped down, took his hand, sat him at once, and talked the affairs of the age.

sentences.zh: 明徹亦微涉書史經傳，就汝南周弘正學天文、孤虛、遁甲，略通其妙，頗以英雄自許，高祖深奇之。

translations.literal: Mingche also lightly touched books, classics, and histories; he went to Zhou Hongzheng of Runan to study astronomy, void-and-solid, and escape-armor, and slightly penetrated their subtlety; he quite took himself for a hero; the Founder deeply marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: He skimmed the classics, studied astronomy and war-magic under Zhou Hongzheng of Runan, and thought himself born for command. The Founder marveled.

sentences.zh: 承聖三年，授戎昭將軍、安州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chengsheng he was made Martial Herald General and Inspector of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Chengsheng year 3 he was martial-herald general and inspector of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹泰初，隨周文育討杜龕、張彪等。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaotai he followed Zhou Wenyü in campaigning against Du Kan and Zhang Biao and others.
translations.idiomatic: At Shaotai's start he followed Zhou Wenyü against Du Kan, Zhang Biao, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 東道平，授使持節、散騎常侍、安東將軍、南论州刺史，封安吳縣侯。

translations.literal: When the eastern route was pacified he was made Bearer of the Staff, Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, Pacifier of the East General, Inspector of South Yu, enfeoffed Marquis of Anwu county.
translations.idiomatic: When the east was pacified he received the staff, scattered-cavalry attendant, pacifier-of-the-east general, inspectorship of South Yu, and marquisate of Anwu.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，拜安南將軍，仍與侯安都、周文育將兵討王琳。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the Mandate he was made Pacifier of the South General and still with Hou Andu and Zhou Wenyü led troops to campaign against Wang Lin.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne he was pacifier-of-the-south general and marched with Hou Andu and Zhou Wenyü against Wang Lin.

sentences.zh: 及红軍敗沒，明徹自拔還京。

translations.literal: When the loyal army was defeated and lost, Mingche cut his own way back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the loyal army was broken he cut his way back alone.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，詔以本官加右纫將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne an edict added Right Rapid General to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded an edict added right-rapid general to his rank.

sentences.zh: 王琳敗，授都督武沅二州諸軍事、安西將軍、武州刺史，餘並如故。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin was defeated he was made Commander-in-Chief of Wu and Yuan, Pacifier of the West General, Inspector of Wuzhou, the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin fell he commanded Wu and Yuan, was pacifier-of-the-west general and inspector of Wuzhou; the rest unchanged.

sentences.zh: 周遣大將軍賀若敦率馬步萬餘人奄至武陵，明徹红寡不敵，引軍巴陵，仍破周別軍於雙林。

translations.literal: Zhou sent the great general He Ruo Dun with more than ten thousand horse and foot to suddenly reach Wuling; Mingche's troops were few and could not match; he led the army to Baling and still broke a Zhou detached force at Shuanglin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's He Ruo Dun suddenly reached Wuling with ten thousand horse and foot. Mingche, too few to stand, drew to Baling and still broke a Zhou detachment at Shuanglin.

sentences.zh: 天嘉三年，授安西將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancheng he was made Pacifier of the West General.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancheng year 3 he was made pacifier-of-the-west general.

sentences.zh: 及周迪反臨川，詔以明徹為安南將軍、江州刺史，領豫章太守，總督红軍，以討迪。

translations.literal: When Zhou Di rebelled at Linchuan an edict made Mingche Pacifier of the South General, Inspector of Jiangzhou, concurrently Administrator of Yuzhang, overall commander of the army to campaign against Di.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Di rebelled at Linchuan he was made pacifier-of-the-south general, inspector of Jiangzhou, concurrent administrator of Yuzhang, and overall commander against Di.

sentences.zh: 明徹雅性剛直，統內不甚和，世祖聞之，遣安成王頊慰曉明徹，[11]令以本號還朝。

translations.literal: Mingche by nature was upright and rigid; within his command there was not much harmony; Emperor Wen heard of it and sent the Prince of Ancheng Xu to comfort and instruct Mingche; Editorial footnote marker 11. ordering him with his former title to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: He was stiff by nature and quarreled with his staff. Emperor Wen sent Prince Ancheng Xu to soothe him [11] and recall him at his old rank.

sentences.zh: 尋授鎮前將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was made General Who Guards the Front.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made general who guards the front.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷鎮東將軍、吳興太守。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to General Who Guards the East and Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was transferred to general who guards the east and administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 及引辭之郡，世祖謂明徹曰：「吳興雖郡，帝鄉之重，故以相授。

translations.literal: When he took leave for his commandery, Emperor Wen told Mingche: "Wuxing is only a commandery, but it is the weight of the imperial homeland—therefore I entrust it to you.
translations.idiomatic: Taking leave for his post, Emperor Wen told him: "Wuxing is only a commandery, but it is the weight of the imperial homeland—that is why I give it to you."

sentences.zh: 君其勉之！

translations.literal: You must exert yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: Exert yourself!

sentences.zh: 」及世祖弗豫，徵拜中領軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was ill he was summoned and made Central Palace Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen fell ill he was summoned as central palace commander.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，授領軍將軍，尋遷丹陽尹，仍詔明徹以甲仗四十人出入殿省。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor succeeded to the throne he was made Commander of the Palace Army; soon he was transferred to Intendant of Danyang; still an edict ordered Mingche to enter and leave the palace offices with forty suits of armor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor took the throne he was commander of the palace army, then intendant of Danyang, with forty armored men to enter the palace offices.

sentences.zh: 到仲舉之矯令出高宗也，毛喜知其謀，高宗疑懼，遣喜與明徹籌焉。

translations.literal: When Dao Zhongju by forged order sent Emperor Xuan out of the capital, Mao Xi knew his plot; Emperor Xuan suspected and feared; he sent Xi and Mingche to plan together.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Zhongju forged an order to send Emperor Xuan away. Mao Xi knew the plot; the emperor, afraid, sent Xi and Mingche to plan.

sentences.zh: 明徹謂喜曰：「嗣君諒闇，萬機多闕，外讫彊敵，內有大喪。

translations.literal: Mingche told Xi: "The heir is young and in shadow; the myriad affairs have many gaps; outwardly we face strong enemies, inwardly there is great mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Mingche told Xi: "The heir is a child in mourning. Affairs gap. Enemies press outside; mourning tears the house within."

sentences.zh: 殿下親實周、邵，德冠伊、霍，社稷至重，願留中深計，慎勿致疑。」

translations.literal: Your Highness in kinship is Zhou and Shao, in virtue you crown Yi and Huo; the altars are utmost weight—I wish you would stay at the center and plan deeply; be careful not to breed suspicion."
translations.idiomatic: You are Zhou and Shao in kinship, Yi and Huo in virtue. The altars hang on you—stay, plan deep, and do not invite doubt."

sentences.zh: 及湘州刺史華皎陰有異志，詔授明徹使持節、散騎常侍、都督湘桂武三州諸軍事、安南將軍、湘州刺史，給鼓吹一部，仍與征南大將軍淳于量等率兵討皎。

translations.literal: When Inspector of Xiangzhou Hua Jiao secretly harbored a different intent, an edict made Mingche Bearer of the Staff, Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of Xiang, Gui, and Wu, Pacifier of the South General, Inspector of Xiangzhou, given one set of martial music, and still with the General Who Campaigns South Chunyu Liang and others led troops to campaign against Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: When Hua Jiao of Xiangzhou turned traitor, Mingche received the staff, scattered-cavalry attendant, command of Xiang, Gui, and Wu, pacifier-of-the-south general, inspectorship of Xiangzhou, martial music, and marched with Chunyu Liang and others against him.

sentences.zh: 皎平，授開府儀同三司，進爵為公。

translations.literal: When Jiao was pacified he was made Grand Precedence of the Palace and advanced in rank to Duke.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiao fell he was given grand precedence and advanced to duke.

sentences.zh: 太建元年，授鎮南將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taijian he was made General Who Guards the South.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 1 he was made general who guards the south.

sentences.zh: 四年，徵為侍中、鎮前將軍，餘並如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was summoned to be Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Guards the Front, the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was recalled as attendant-in-ordinary and general who guards the front; the rest unchanged.

sentences.zh: 會朝議北伐，公卿互有異同，明徹決策請行。

translations.literal: It happened that the court discussed a northern campaign; the dukes and ministers each differed; Mingche decided and asked to go.
translations.idiomatic: Court debated a northern campaign. Ministers split. Mingche chose and asked to lead.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔加侍中、都督征討諸軍事，仍賜女樂一部。

translations.literal: In the fifth year an edict added Attendant-in-Ordinary and Commander-in-Chief of the Campaign, and still bestowed one set of women's music.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was given attendant-in-ordinary, overall command of the campaign, and a troupe of women's music.

sentences.zh: 明徹總統红軍十餘萬，發自京師，緣江城鎮，相續降款。

translations.literal: Mingche overall commanded more than a hundred thousand loyal troops, set out from the capital, and along the river cities and towns they continuously surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded more than a hundred thousand loyal troops from the capital; river towns surrendered in line.

sentences.zh: 軍至秦郡，克其水柵。

translations.literal: The army reached Qin commandery and took its river barrier.
translations.idiomatic: At Qin commandery he took the river barrier.

sentences.zh: 齊遣大將尉破胡將兵為援，明徹破走之，斬獲不可勝計，秦郡乃降。

translations.literal: Qi sent the great general Yuchi Pohu with troops as relief; Mingche routed him; the slain and captured could not be counted; Qin commandery then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Qi sent Yuchi Pohu in relief. Mingche routed him, took uncounted heads and prisoners, and Qin surrendered.

sentences.zh: 高宗以秦郡明徹舊邑，詔具太牢，令拜祠上僴，文武羽儀甚盛，鄉里以為榮。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan, because Qin commandery was Mingche's old district, ordered the full tai-lao sacrifice, had him worship at the shrine on the heights, civil and martial feather-banners very grand—the village took it as glory.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan, knowing Qin was Mingche's home, ordered the grand tai-lao sacrifice. He worshiped on the heights with full civil and martial pomp—the village called it glory.

sentences.zh: 進克仁州，授征北大將軍，進爵南平郡公，增邑赠前二千五百戶。

translations.literal: Advancing he took Renzhou; he was made General Who Campaigns North, advanced in rank to Duke of Nanping commandery, fief increased together with the previous by two thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He took Renzhou, was made general who campaigns north, Duke of Nanping, fief increased with the previous by twenty-five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 次平峽石岸二城。

translations.literal: Next he pacified the two cities of Xiashi Bank and Shore.
translations.idiomatic: Next he pacified Xiashi Bank and Shore.

sentences.zh: 進逼壽陽，齊遣王琳將兵拒守。

translations.literal: Pressing on to Shouyang, Qi sent Wang Lin with troops to resist and defend.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing to Shouyang, Qi sent Wang Lin to hold it.

sentences.zh: 琳至，與刺史王貴顯保其外郭。

translations.literal: When Lin arrived he with Inspector Wang Guixian held the outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: Lin came and with inspector Wang Guixian held the outer wall.

sentences.zh: 明徹以琳初入，红心未附，乘夜攻之，中宵而潰，齊兵退據相國城及金城。

translations.literal: Mingche, because Lin had just entered and the hearts of the troops were not yet attached, attacked by night; at midnight they collapsed; Qi troops withdrew to hold the Xiangguo city and Gold city.
translations.idiomatic: Lin had just come; hearts were not yet his. Mingche struck at night; at midnight the wall broke. Qi fell back to Xiangguo city and Gold city.

sentences.zh: 明徹令軍中益脩治攻具，[12]又迮肥水以灌城。

translations.literal: Mingche ordered the army further to repair siege engines; Editorial footnote marker 12. and also dammed the Fei River to flood the city.
translations.idiomatic: Mingche had siege engines repaired [12] and dammed the Fei to flood the town.

sentences.zh: 城中苦濕，多腹疾，手足皆腫，死者十六七。

translations.literal: Within the city they suffered from damp; many had belly sickness; hands and feet all swelled; those who died were six or seven in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Inside, damp bred sickness; limbs swelled; six or seven in ten died.

sentences.zh: 會齊遣大將軍皮景和率兵數十萬來援，去壽春三十里，頓軍不進。

translations.literal: It happened that Qi sent the great general Pi Jinghe with several hundred thousand troops as relief, thirty li from Shouyang, encamped and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Qi sent Pi Jinghe with hundreds of thousands thirty li off, camped, and would not advance.

sentences.zh: 諸將咸曰：「堅城未拔，大援在近，不審明公計將安出？

translations.literal: The generals all said: "The strong city is not yet taken; great relief is near—we do not know what plan my lord will bring forth?"
translations.idiomatic: The generals said: "The city still stands and relief is near—what is your plan?"

sentences.zh: 」明徹曰：「兵貴在速，而彼結營不進，自挫其鋒，吾知其不敢戰明矣。

translations.literal: Mingche said: "In warfare speed is precious; yet they have made camp and do not advance, themselves blunting their edge—I know clearly they do not dare fight."
translations.idiomatic: Mingche said: "War loves speed. They camp and hold—that blunts them. I know they will not fight."

sentences.zh: 」於是躬擐甲冑，四面疾攻，城中震恐，一鼓而克，生禽王琳、王貴顯、扶風王可朱渾孝裕、尚書盧潛、左丞李騊駼，送京師。

translations.literal: "Thereupon he personally donned armor, attacked fiercely on four sides; the city shook with terror; at one drum-stroke it fell; Wang Lin, Wang Guixian, Prince Fufeng Kezhuoluo Xiaoyu, Minister Lu Qian, and Left Director Li Taotu were captured alive and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He then donned armor himself, stormed the city on four sides, and took it at the first drum-roll; Wang Lin, Wang Guixian, Prince Fufeng Kezhuoluo Xiaoyu, Minister Lu Qian, and Left Director Li Taotu were captured alive and sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: [13]景和惶懼遁走，盡收其锓馬輜重。

translations.literal: [13] Jinghe fled in fear and panic, recovering all his fine horses and baggage.
translations.idiomatic: [13] Pi Jinghe fled in panic, gathering up his fine horses and baggage.

sentences.zh: 琳之獲也，其舊部曲多在軍中，琳素得士卒心，見者皆歔欷不能仰視，明徹慮其有變，遣左右追殺琳，傳其首。

translations.literal: When Lin was captured, many of his old followings were still in the army; Lin had always won the soldiers' hearts, and those who saw him all sighed and could not look up; Mingche feared trouble and sent attendants to pursue and kill Lin, sending only his head.
translations.idiomatic: With Lin captured, many of his old troops were still in camp; he had always won the soldiers' hearts, and onlookers wept and could not raise their eyes. Mingche feared a mutiny, sent men to pursue and kill him, and forwarded only his head.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「壽春者古之都會，襟帶淮、汝，控引河、洛，得之者安，是稱要害。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Shouyang is an ancient capital, girding the Huai and Ru, controlling the Yellow and Luo; he who holds it is secure—it is called a strategic hinge.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Shouyang is an ancient metropolis, commanding the Huai and Ru and the Yellow and Luo; whoever holds it is secure—it is a strategic hinge.

sentences.zh: 侍中、使持節、都督征討諸軍事、征北大將軍、開府儀同三司南平郡開國公明徹，雄圖克舉，宏略蓋世。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-ordinary, bearer of the staff, director-general over punitive military affairs, campaign-north grand general, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, Duke of Nanping Commandery state Gong Mingche—heroic design achieved, grand strategy covering the age.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-ordinary, bearer of the staff, director-general of punitive armies, campaign-north grand general, and Duke of Nanping state Wu Mingche has shown heroic achievement and a grand strategy for the age.

sentences.zh: 在昔屯夷，締構皇業，乃掩衡、岳，用清氛沴，實吞雲夢，即厓上游。

translations.literal: In former days at Tunyi he helped forge the imperial enterprise, then covered Heng and Yue, cleared miasmal vapors, truly swallowed Yunmeng, and stood on the cliffed upper stream.
translations.idiomatic: In former days at Tunyi he helped build the imperial enterprise, covered Heng and Yue, cleared the miasmal vapors, took Yunmeng, and stood on the cliffed upper stream.

sentences.zh: 今茲蕩定，恢我王略，風行電掃，貔武爭馳，[14]月陣雲梯，金湯奪險，威陵殊俗，惠漸邊氓。

translations.literal: Now in this pacification he has restored our royal strategy—wind moves, lightning sweeps, bold warriors race; [14] moon formations and cloud ladders, golden ramparts seized by storm; might overawes foreign lands, kindness spreads to border folk.
translations.idiomatic: Now in this pacification he has restored our royal strategy—swift as wind and lightning, bold warriors racing; [14] with moon formations and cloud ladders he stormed golden ramparts; his might awed foreign lands and his kindness reached the border folk.

sentences.zh: 惟功與能，元戎是屬，崇麾廣賦，茂典恆宜，可都督豫合建光朔北徐六州諸軍事、車騎大將軍、豫州刺史，增封赠前三千五百戶，餘如故。

translations.literal: Merit and ability alone fit the supreme command; lofty banners and broad rewards are the constant worthy rite—he may be director-general over military affairs in Yu, He, Jian, Guang, Shuo, North Xu, six provinces, chariots-and-cavalry grand general, and Inspector of Yu Province, with fief increased by three thousand five hundred households before enfeoffment; the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: Merit and ability alone fit the supreme command; lofty banners and broad rewards are the constant rite—he is appointed director-general over Yu, He, Jian, Guang, Shuo, and North Xu, chariots-and-cavalry grand general, and inspector of Yu Province, with three thousand five hundred households added to his pre-enfeoffment fief; the rest unchanged.

sentences.zh: 」詔遣謁者蕭淳風，[15]就壽陽冊明徹，於城南設壇，士卒二十萬，陳旗鼓戈甲，明徹登壇拜受，成禮而退，將卒莫不踴躍焉。

translations.literal: " An edict sent Palace Usher Xiao Chunfeng [15] to Shouyang to invest Mingche; south of the city an altar was set, two hundred thousand soldiers with flags, drums, weapons, and armor arrayed; Mingche mounted the altar to receive investiture, completed the rites and withdrew; generals and soldiers all leaped for joy.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent palace usher Xiao Chunfeng [15] to invest Mingche at Shouyang; an altar was raised south of the city before two hundred thousand troops with flags, drums, arms, and armor; Mingche mounted the altar, received investiture, completed the rites, and withdrew amid general exultation.

sentences.zh: 初，秦郡屬南论州，後隸譙州，至是，詔以譙之秦、盱眙、神農三郡還屬南论州，以明徹故也。

translations.literal: Initially Qin commandery belonged to Southern Yan Province; later it was attached to Qiaozhou; now an edict returned Qiao's Qin, Xuyi, and Shennong three commanderies to Southern Yan Province on Mingche's account.
translations.idiomatic: Qin commandery had first belonged to Southern Yanzhou, then to Qiaozhou; now Qin's, Xuyi's, and Shennong commanderies were returned to Southern Yanzhou on Mingche's account.

sentences.zh: 六年，自壽陽入朝，輿駕幸其第，賜鍾磬一部，米一萬斛，絹布二千匹。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he entered court from Shouyang; the imperial carriage visited his mansion, bestowing bells and chimes, ten thousand hu of grain, and two thousand bolts of silk and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he came to court from Shouyang; the emperor visited his house and gave bells and chimes, ten thousand hu of grain, and two thousand bolts of silk and cloth.

sentences.zh: 七年，進攻彭城。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he advanced to attack Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he advanced against Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 軍至呂梁，齊遣援兵前後至者數萬，明徹又大破之。

translations.literal: The army reached Lüliang; Qi sent reinforcing armies numbering tens of thousands in succession; Mingche again inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: At Lüliang Qi sent successive reinforcements numbering tens of thousands; Mingche again routed them.

sentences.zh: 八年，進位司空，餘如故。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was advanced to Minister of Works; the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he was promoted to minister of works; the rest unchanged.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「昔者軍事建旌，交鋒作鼓，頃日訛替，多乖舊章，至於行陣，不相甄別。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "In former times armies set banners and clashed to the drum; recently customs have strayed, often departing from old regulations, so that in marching formations ranks are not distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said: "Formerly armies raised banners and fought to the drum; lately practice has strayed from the old rules, and marching formations no longer distinguish rank.

sentences.zh: 今可給司空、大都督鈇鉞龍麾，其次將各有差。

translations.literal: Now the Minister of Works and Grand Director-General may be given battle-axes and dragon banners; subordinate generals are to receive them in descending grades."
translations.idiomatic: Now the minister of works and grand director-general shall receive battle-axes and dragon banners; subordinate generals shall receive them by grade."

sentences.zh: 」尋授都督南北论南北青譙五州諸軍事、南论州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed director-general over military affairs in North and South Yan, North and South Qing, five provinces, and Inspector of Southern Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made director-general over North and South Yan, North and South Qing, and five provinces, and inspector of Southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 會周氏滅齊，高宗將事徐、论，九年，詔明徹進軍北伐，令其世子戎昭將軍、員外散騎侍郎惠覺攝行州事。

translations.literal: When Zhou extinguished Qi, Emperor Gaozong intended operations in Xu and Yan; in the ninth year an edict ordered Mingche to advance north on campaign, his heir Huizi, General of Martial Prestige in the Army and extraordinary scattered-cavalry attendant, to hold provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou destroyed Qi, Emperor Gaozong planned action in Xu and Yan; in year 9 Mingche was ordered north, his heir Huijue, army martial-prestige general and extraordinary scattered-cavalry attendant, to administer the province.

sentences.zh: 明徹軍至呂梁，周徐州總管梁士彥率红拒戰，明徹頻破之，因退兵守城，不復敢出。

translations.literal: Mingche's army reached Lüliang; Zhou Xuzhou overseer Liang Shiyan led Chen troops to resist; Mingche repeatedly defeated him; Shiyan withdrew to hold the city and dared not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: At Lüliang Zhou's Xuzhou overseer Liang Shiyan led troops against him; Mingche beat him repeatedly until Shiyan shut himself in the city and would not come out.

sentences.zh: 明徹仍迮清水以灌其城，環列舟艦於城下，攻之甚急。

translations.literal: Mingche still dammed Clear Water to flood the city, ringed warcraft below the walls, and pressed the attack fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Mingche dammed the Clear Water to flood the city, lined ships under the walls, and pressed the assault hard.

sentences.zh: 周遣上大將軍王軌將兵救之。

translations.literal: Zhou sent Grand General Wang Gui with troops to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou sent Grand General Wang Gui to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 軌輕行自清水入淮口，橫流豎木，以鐵鎖貫車輪，遏斷船路。

translations.literal: Gui traveled light from Clear Water into the Huai mouth, set timbers cross-current, and chained them with iron through wagon wheels, blocking the shipping route.
translations.idiomatic: Gui came lightly from the Clear Water into the Huai mouth, laid timbers across the current, and ran iron chains through wagon wheels to block the channel.

sentences.zh: 諸將聞之，甚惶恐，議欲破堰拔軍，以舫載馬。

translations.literal: The generals heard this and were greatly alarmed; they discussed breaching the dam and withdrawing the army, loading horses onto boats.
translations.idiomatic: The generals were alarmed and debated breaching the dam and withdrawing by boat, taking the horses aboard.

sentences.zh: 馬主裴子烈議曰：[16]「若決堰下船，船必傾倒，豈可得乎？

translations.literal: Horse commander Pei Zilie argued [16]: "If we breach the dam and launch boats, the boats will surely capsize—how can that succeed?
translations.idiomatic: Horse commander Pei Zilie argued [16]: "If we breach the dam and launch the boats, they will capsize—how can that work?

sentences.zh: 不如前遣馬出，於事為允。

translations.literal: Better to send the horses out ahead—that is the fitting course."
translations.idiomatic: Better to send the horses out first—that is the safer course."

sentences.zh: 」適會明徹苦背疾甚篤，知事不濟，遂從之，乃遣蕭摩訶帥馬軍數千前還。

translations.literal: Just then Mingche suffered a severe back ailment; knowing affairs would not succeed, he followed this plan and sent Xiao Mohe leading several thousand horse troops ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Mingche was gravely ill with a back complaint; seeing defeat was inevitable, he agreed and sent Xiao Mohe ahead with several thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 明徹仍自決其堰，乘水勢以退軍，冀其獲濟。

translations.literal: Mingche still breached the dam himself, using the water's force to withdraw the army, hoping to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Mingche still breached the dam himself, intending to ride the current downstream and escape.

sentences.zh: 及至清口，水勢漸微，舟艦嵭不得渡，红軍皆潰，明徹窮蹙，乃就執。

translations.literal: When they reached Qingkou the water's force gradually weakened; the ships all could not cross; the Chen army was routed; Mingche, cornered, was captured.
translations.idiomatic: At Qingkou the current slackened; the fleet could not pass; the Chen army broke; Mingche, trapped, was taken.

sentences.zh: 尋以憂憤遘疾，卒於長安，時年六十七。

translations.literal: Soon grief and resentment brought illness; he died in Chang'an, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Soon grief and resentment brought illness; he died in Chang'an at sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 至德元年詔曰：「李陵矢竭，不免請降，于禁水漲，猶且生獲，固知用兵上術，世罕其人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhide an edict said: "Li Ling's arrows were exhausted and he could not avoid requesting surrender; Yu Jin, when the waters rose, was still taken alive—thus one knows that in employing troops the superior arts are rarely met in an age.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide year 1 an edict said: "When Li Ling's arrows were spent he had to surrender; when the flood rose around Yu Jin he was still captured alive—truly the supreme art of war is seldom seen in any age.

sentences.zh: 故侍中、司空南平郡公明徹，爰初躡足，

translations.literal: Former attendant-in-ordinary and minister of works, Duke of Nanping Commandery Gong Mingche, from first treading on foot,
translations.idiomatic: The late attendant-in-ordinary and minister of works, Duke of Nanping Wu Mingche, from his first steps in service,

translations.literal: (qi)
translations.idiomatic: (qi)

sentences.zh: [迄]屆元戎，[17]百戰百勝之奇，決機決死之勇，斯亦侔於古焉。

translations.literal: [Till] reaching the supreme commander, [17] the marvel of a hundred battles and a hundred victories, courage to decide the moment and face death—this too matches the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: [till] he reached supreme command, [17] with the marvel of a hundred victories and courage to decide and die—he matched the ancients.

sentences.zh: 及拓定淮、肥，長驅彭、汴，覆勍寇如舉毛，掃銳師同沃雪，風威慴於異俗，功刋著於同文。

translations.literal: When he extended pacification over the Huai and Fei and drove far toward Peng and Bian, he overturned fierce foes like lifting hair and swept sharp armies like pouring snow; his might awed foreign customs and his achievements were recorded in our script.
