translations.idiomatic: Pacifying the Huai and Fei and driving deep toward Peng and Bian, he overturned fierce foes like plucking hair and swept elite armies like melting snow; his might awed foreign lands and his deeds were written in our script.

sentences.zh: 方欲息駕陰山，解鞍澣海，既而師出已老，數亦終奇，不就結纓之功，無辭入褚之屈，望封崤之為易，冀平翟之非難，雖志在屈伸，而奄中霜露，埋恨絕域，甚可嗟傷。

translations.literal: Just when he was about to rest his chariot at Yinshan and unstrap his saddle at Huanhai, the armies went forth already aged and fate's count also ended its marvel; he did not achieve the merit of knotting the tassel and could not avoid the humiliation of entering the ward; he hoped making Feng and Xiao easy and expected pacifying Di not to be hard—though his will bent and stretched, suddenly he met frost and dew mid-course; buried grievance in a distant realm—very lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was to rest his chariot at Yinshan and unstrap at Huanhai, his armies grew old on campaign and fortune's tally ran out; he won no knotting-the-cord merit and could not escape the shame of captivity; he thought taking Feng and Xiao would be easy and pacifying Di not hard—yet though his will bent and straightened, frost and dew struck him suddenly; he died with grievance in a distant land—deeply to be mourned.

sentences.zh: 斯事已往，累逢肆赦，凡厥罪戾，皆蒙洒濯，獨此孤魂，未霑寬惠，遂使爵土湮沒，饗醊無主。

translations.literal: This affair is already past and amnesties have repeatedly been proclaimed; all crimes and guilt have received sprinkling and washing, yet this lonely soul alone has not touched broad grace, so that fief and lands are submerged and sacrifices have no master.
translations.idiomatic: That affair is past and repeated amnesties have washed all guilt, yet this lone soul alone received no grace, so his fief lies vacant and his sacrifices have no master.

sentences.zh: 笃瑕錄用，宜在茲辰，可追封邵陵縣開國侯，食邑一千戶，以其息惠覺為嗣。」

translations.literal: Recording the flawed for employment is fitting at this season; he may be posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Shaoling county state, fief one thousand households, with his son Huijue as heir."
translations.idiomatic: To raise the flawed for service is fitting now; he is posthumously enfeoffed as marquis of Shaoling county, fief one thousand households, with his son Huijue as heir."

sentences.zh: 惠覺歷黃門侍郎，以平章大寶功，授豐州刺史。

translations.literal: Huijue served as gentleman of the yellow gate; for merit in pacifying Zhang Dabao he was appointed Inspector of Feng Province.
translations.idiomatic: Huijue rose to gentleman of the yellow gate; for pacifying Zhang Dabao he was made inspector of Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 明徹兄子超，字逸世。

translations.literal: Mingche's nephew Chao, styled Yishi.
translations.idiomatic: Mingche's nephew Chao, styled Yishi.

sentences.zh: 少倜儻，以幹灯知名。

translations.literal: In youth he was bold and unrestrained, known for capability.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was bold and capable.

sentences.zh: 隨明徹征伐，有戰功，官至忠毅將軍、散騎常侍、桂州刺史，封汝南縣侯，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: Following Mingche on campaigns he had military merit, reaching Loyal-and-Steadfast General, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, Inspector of Gui Province, and Marquis of Runan county, fief one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned with Mingche with merit, reaching loyal-and-steadfast general, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, inspector of Guizhou, and marquis of Runan with one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈廣州刺史，謚曰節。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Inspector of Guang Province, posthumous title Jie.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously made inspector of Guangzhou, posthumous title Jie.

sentences.zh: 裴子烈字大士，河東聞喜人，梁員外散騎常侍猗之子。

translations.literal: Pei Zilie, styled Dashi, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong, son of Liang extraordinary scattered-cavalry attendant Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zilie, styled Dashi, was from Wenxi in Hedong, son of Liang extraordinary scattered-cavalry attendant Yi.

sentences.zh: 子烈少孤，有志氣。

translations.literal: Zilie was orphaned young and had resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Zilie lost his father young and had strong resolve.

sentences.zh: 遇梁末喪亂，因習武藝，以驍勇聞。

translations.literal: Meeting the disorders at the end of Liang, he took up martial arts and was known for fierce courage.
translations.idiomatic: In the disorders at the end of Liang he took up arms and was known for fierce courage.

sentences.zh: 頻從明徹征討，所向必先登陷陣。

translations.literal: He repeatedly followed Mingche on punitive campaigns, always first to scale walls and break formations.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Mingche on campaign again and again, always first over the wall and into the line.

sentences.zh: 官至電威將軍、北譙太守、岳陽內史，海安縣伯，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: He reached Lightning Prestige General, Administrator of North Qiao, and Interior Minister of Yueyang, Baron of Hai'an county, fief three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He reached lightning-prestige general, administrator of North Qiao, interior minister of Yueyang, and baron of Hai'an with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: [18]至德四年卒。

translations.literal: [18] In the fourth year of Zhide he died.
translations.idiomatic: [18] He died in Zhide year 4.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：高祖撥亂創基，光啟天曆，侯瑱、歐陽頠嵭歸身有道，位貴鼎司，美矣。

translations.literal: The historian says: The High Ancestor ordered chaos and founded the foundation, broadly opening Heaven's fortune; Hou Tian and Ouyang Wei fully gave themselves to the Way, posts honored to the tripartite minister—beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: The High Ancestor quelled chaos and opened the mandate; Hou Tian and Ouyang Wei gave themselves wholly to the throne and rose to the highest offices—admirable.

sentences.zh: 吳明徹居將帥之任，初有軍功，及呂梁敗績，為失筭也。

translations.literal: Wu Mingche held a commander's charge; at first he had military merit; at the Lüliang defeat it was miscalculation.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mingche held command; at first he won battles; at Lüliang he miscalculated.

sentences.zh: 斯以勇非韓、白，識異孫、吳，遂使蹙境喪師，金陵虛弱，禎明淪覆，蓋由其漸焉。

translations.literal: Thus his courage was not like Han Xin or Bai Qi, his wisdom unlike Sun or Wu—therefore borders were cramped, armies lost, Jinling weakened, and Zhenming fell—largely from this gradual slope.
translations.idiomatic: His courage was not Han Xin's or Bai Qi's, his wisdom not Sun Wu's—borders shrank, armies were lost, Jinling grew weak, and Zhenming fell, largely from this beginning.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 以應

translations.literal: to answer
translations.idiomatic: to answer

translations.idiomatic: (wo)

sentences.zh: [義]軍 據北監本、汲本、殿本及《元龜》七六一改。

translations.literal: [yi] the army—changed according to the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, Hall editions and Comprehensive Mirror 761.
translations.idiomatic: [yi] the army—emended per the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions and Comprehensive Mirror 761.

sentences.zh: 按《南史》作「以應義師」。

translations.literal: Comment: the Southern History reads "to answer the righteous army."
translations.idiomatic: Note: the Southern History reads "to answer the righteous army."

sentences.zh: 除使持節鎮北將軍 按《梁書·元帝紀》，承聖三年春正月甲午，加南豫州刺史侯瑱征北將軍。

translations.literal: Removed as bearer of the staff, Pacifies-North General—comment: in the Basic Annals of Emperor Yuan of Liang, third year of Chengsheng, first month, jiawu day, Southern Yuzhou Inspector Hou Tian was advanced to Campaign-North General; here it reads Pacifies-North General—probably an error.
translations.idiomatic: On "removed as bearer of the staff, pacifies-north general": Liang Emperor Yuan's annals for Chengsheng year 3, first month, jiawu, advance Southern Yuzhou inspector Hou Tian to campaign-north general; pacifies-north here is probably wrong.

sentences.zh: 此作「鎮北將軍」，恐誤。

translations.literal: This reads Pacifies-North General—probably an error.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifies-north general is probably an error.

sentences.zh: 奫與其部下俟方兒不協 「俟」北監本、汲本、殿本及《南史》、《元龜》二〇九、四五〇並作「侯」。

translations.literal: Ao and his subordinate Hou Fang'er were not in accord—"Hou" in the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, Hall editions and Southern History and Comprehensive Mirror 209 and 450 all read "Marquis."
translations.idiomatic: On "Ao and his subordinate Hou Fang'er were not in accord": the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, Hall editions, Southern History, and Comprehensive Mirror 209 and 450 read Marquis for Hou.

sentences.zh: 瑱率軍進獸檻洲 按「獸檻洲」即「虎檻洲」，避唐諱改。

translations.literal: Tian led the army to advance to Beast-barrier Isle—comment: "Beast-barrier Isle" is "Tiger-barrier Isle," changed to avoid Tang taboo.
translations.idiomatic: On "Tian led the army to Beast-barrier Isle": Beast-barrier is Tiger-barrier, changed for Tang taboo.

sentences.zh: 分搥盪頓蕪湖洲尾以待之 《南史》無「分搥盪」三字。

translations.literal: divided hammer-strike and halted at the tail of Wuhu Isle to await them—the Southern History lacks the three characters "divided hammer-strike."
translations.idiomatic: On "divided hammer-strike and halted at the tail of Wuhu Isle": the Southern History lacks divided hammer-strike.

sentences.zh: 按「分搥盪」三字疑衍。

translations.literal: Comment: the three characters "divided hammer-strike" are suspected as interpolation.
translations.idiomatic: Note: divided hammer-strike looks like an interpolation.

sentences.zh: 或衍「槌盪」二字，本卷後附舊校云或本作「分頓」，是曾鞏等所見本有作「分頓蕪湖洲尾」者。

translations.literal: Or the two characters "hammer-strike" are suspected as interpolation; the old collation appended at the end of this scroll says the text may originally have read "divided halt," showing that the edition seen by Zeng Gong and others had "divided halt at the tail of Wuhu Isle."
translations.idiomatic: Or hammer-strike is interpolated; old collation at the scroll's end says the text may read divided halt, as in editions Zeng Gong saw.

sentences.zh: 又：

translations.literal: Also:
translations.idiomatic: Also:

sentences.zh: 〈侯瑱傳〉

translations.literal: 〈Biography of Hou Tian〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Biography of Hou Tian〉

sentences.zh: 「分搥盪頓蕪湖洲尾」，或本作「分頓」，疑。

translations.literal: "divided hammer-strike and halted at the tail of Wuhu Isle"—the text may originally have read "divided halt"—doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: "divided hammer-strike and halted at the tail of Wuhu Isle"—or divided halt—doubtful.

sentences.zh: 乃與妻妾左右十餘人入齊 「乃」各本訛「及」。

translations.literal: then entered Qi with his wife, concubines, and more than ten attendants—"then" in all editions is corrupted to "and."
translations.idiomatic: On "then entered Qi with wife, concubines, and attendants": all editions corrupt then to and.

sentences.zh: 殿本考證云：「上文謂王琳走至湓城，红無附者，故遂入齊，此『及』字係『乃』字之訛也。

translations.literal: The Hall edition's textual verification says: "Above it says Wang Lin fled to Pencheng and Chen troops would not attach to him, therefore he entered Qi—this character 'and' is a corruption for 'then.'"
translations.idiomatic: The Hall edition notes: above, Wang Lin reached Pencheng and Chen troops would not follow, so he entered Qi—and is a corruption of then.

sentences.zh: 」按《南史》正作「乃」，今據改。

translations.literal: Comment: the Southern History correctly reads "then"; now changed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Note: the Southern History reads then; emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 蘭欽弟前高州刺史裕攻始興內史蕭紹基 按「蕭紹基」《南史》作「蕭昭基」。

translations.literal: Lan Qin's younger brother, former Inspector of High Province Yu, attacked Shixing Interior Minister Xiao Shaoji—comment: "Xiao Shaoji" in the Southern History reads "Xiao Zhaoji."
translations.idiomatic: On "Lan Qin's brother, former High Province inspector Yu, attacked Shixing interior minister Xiao Shaoji": the Southern History reads Xiao Zhaoji.

sentences.zh: 恐蕭廣州不肯致之 「致」字原缺，據各本補。

translations.literal: fearing the Inspector of Guangzhou would not send him—"send" was originally missing and is supplied according to all editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "fearing the Guangzhou inspector would not send him": send was missing and is supplied from all editions.

sentences.zh: 令以百兩還合浦太守龔蒍 按「龔蒍」《南史》作「襲蒍」。

translations.literal: ordered one hundred taels returned to Hepu Administrator Gong Ai—comment: "Gong Ai" in the Southern History reads "Xi Ai."
translations.idiomatic: On "ordered one hundred taels returned to Hepu administrator Gong Ai": the Southern History reads Xi Ai.

sentences.zh: 吳明徹字通昭 「通昭」《南史》作「通炤」。

translations.literal: Wu Mingche, styled Tongzhao—"Tongzhao" in the Southern History reads "Tongzhao" with the fire radical.
translations.idiomatic: On "Wu Mingche, styled Tongzhao": the Southern History reads Tongzhao with the fire radical.

sentences.zh: 按本卷後附舊校云或本作「通炤」，是曾鞏等所見本亦有作「炤」者。

translations.literal: Comment: the old collation appended at the end of this scroll says the text may originally have read "Tongzhao" with the fire radical, showing that the edition seen by Zeng Gong and others also had zhao with that radical.
translations.idiomatic: Old collation at the scroll's end says the text may read Tongzhao with the fire radical, as in Zeng Gong's edition.

sentences.zh: 又：「吳明徹字通昭」，或本作「通炤」，疑。

translations.literal: Also: "Wu Mingche, styled Tongzhao"—the text may originally have read "Tongzhao" with the fire radical—doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Also: "Wu Mingche, styled Tongzhao"—or Tongzhao with the fire radical—doubtful.

sentences.zh: 遣安成王頊慰曉明徹 「頊」原作「諱」，以姚察曾仕陳，故避陳諱，今依殿本改。

translations.literal: sent Prince of Ancheng Xu to console and instruct Mingche—"Xu" was originally written "taboo name"; because Yao Cha once served Chen, Chen taboo was avoided; now changed according to the Hall edition.
translations.idiomatic: On "sent Prince of Ancheng Xu to console Mingche": Xu was written taboo name because Yao Cha served Chen; emended per the Hall edition.

sentences.zh: 明徹令軍中益脩治攻具 「治」字原缺，據各本補。

translations.literal: Mingche ordered the army further to repair siege engines—"repair" was originally missing and is supplied according to all editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "Mingche ordered the army to repair siege engines": repair was missing and is supplied from all editions.

sentences.zh: 生禽王琳至送京師 「可朱渾孝裕」《通鑑》陳宣帝太建五年作「可朱渾道裕」。

translations.literal: captured Wang Lin alive and sent to the capital—"Kezhuoluo Xiaoyu" in Comprehensive Mirror, Chen Emperor Xuan's fifth year of Taijian, reads "Kezhuoluo Daoyu."
translations.idiomatic: On "captured Wang Lin alive and sent to the capital": Comprehensive Mirror, Chen Emperor Xuan Taijian year 5, reads Kezhuoluo Daoyu for Kezhuoluo Xiaoyu.

sentences.zh: 按齊被俘諸將姓名，《北齊書》及《南史》均多缺略。

translations.literal: Comment: the names of Qi commanders taken prisoner in Northern Qi History and Southern History are mostly abbreviated.
translations.idiomatic: Note: captured Qi commanders' names are mostly abbreviated in the Northern Qi History and Southern History.

sentences.zh: 《元龜》三六八亦作「孝裕」，《通鑑》作「道裕」，未知何據。

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror 368 also reads "Xiaoyu"; Comprehensive Mirror reads "Daoyu"—the basis is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror 368 also has Xiaoyu; another passage has Daoyu—the basis is unknown.

sentences.zh: 貔武爭馳 「武」北監本、殿本作「虎」。

translations.literal: bold warriors racing—"warrior" in the Northern Supervisory and Hall editions reads "tiger."
translations.idiomatic: On "bold warriors racing": the Northern Supervisory and Hall editions read tiger for warrior.

sentences.zh: 按此避唐諱改。

translations.literal: Comment: this was changed to avoid Tang taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Note: changed for Tang taboo.

sentences.zh: 詔遣謁者蕭淳風 「蕭淳風」《南史》作「蕭淳」。

translations.literal: An edict sent Palace Usher Xiao Chunfeng—"Xiao Chunfeng" in the Southern History reads "Xiao Chun."
translations.idiomatic: On "edict sent palace usher Xiao Chunfeng": the Southern History reads Xiao Chun.

sentences.zh: 馬主裴子烈議曰 「馬主」《南史》作「馬明戍」。

translations.literal: Horse commander Pei Zilie argued—"horse commander" in the Southern History reads "horse bright garrison."
translations.idiomatic: On "horse commander Pei Zilie argued": the Southern History reads horse bright garrison.

sentences.zh: 按《通鑑》陳宣帝太建十年作「馬主」，考異云《南史》作「馬明主」，今從陳書。

translations.literal: Comment: Comprehensive Mirror, Chen Emperor Xuan's tenth year of Taijian, reads "horse commander"; Examination of Variants says the Southern History reads "horse bright commander"—now following the Book of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror, Chen Emperor Xuan Taijian year 10, reads horse commander; Examination of Variants says the Southern History reads horse bright commander—following the Book of Chen.

translations.literal: (qi)
translations.idiomatic: (qi)

sentences.zh: [迄]屆元戎 據北監本、殿本改。

translations.literal: [Till] reaching the supreme commander—changed according to the Northern Supervisory and Hall editions.
translations.idiomatic: [Till] reaching the supreme commander—emended per the Northern Supervisory and Hall editions.

sentences.zh: 邑三百戶 各本作「五百戶」。

translations.literal: fief three hundred households—all editions read "five hundred households."
translations.idiomatic: On "fief three hundred households": all editions read five hundred households.
